source.title: Alleviating the Fear of Losing Alignment in LLM Fine-tuning
source.authors: Kang Yang; Guan-Hong Tao; Xun Chen; Jun Xu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes aligned models on harmful or benign task data and measures harmful-answer rates, directly testing the fine-tuning and safety-behavior relationship.
record.gate_note: The study also evaluates alignment recovery and direction interventions. Its SoftSFT discussion and comparison do not test whether prefilling a compliant opening, suffixes, or decoding changes bypass safety; the paper reports no per-token KL measurement. Prior-work results quoted in Related Work are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: The motivating study (§3, Table 3) and the pure-harmful study (§7, Table 6) fine-tune five aligned chat models on harmful, mixed, or clean task data and measure BeaverTails/HEx-PHI harmful rates. This directly tests V1 and V2. The selective weight-restoration results bear on V5, and the SoftSFT baseline comparison (Figure 4) bears on V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that fine-tuning, even on clean data, can compromise alignment, and that their gradient-guided restoration of a small subset of weights (with rollback) recovers alignment with about 2.9% task-performance loss. They also conclude that this beats SoftSFT, which they say is insufficient because it constrains only the first tokens, and RESTA, which hurts task performance. Note that clean-data erosion was observed only in Mistral and Qwen.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests the fine-tuning/safety relationship with QLoRA across five base models and several task datasets, and includes harmful-data injection and pure-harmful-data fine-tuning. It is not presented as an explicit replication of the original study's exact setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies by model, task dataset, amount of injected harmful data, and harmful-rate evaluation dataset. For recovery, the paper also reports sensitivity to direction-layer position and some recovery settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Shifting the last-token hidden state at layer 2/3 toward a benign-prompt mean and away from a harmful-prompt mean raises the harmful rate from about 0–12% to 45–82%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal in aligned models is mediated by a mean-difference activation direction whose manipulation removes safety.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (2025)
record.problems: The reported harmful-rate results have no uncertainty intervals or significance tests stated. Harmfulness is judged using a model fine-tuned by ShieldLLM. Some recovery analyses are presented in figures, but the extracted fine-tuning outcomes above are tabulated or explicitly stated.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many additional fine-tuning conditions in Table 3 and recovery outcomes in Figures 3–7 and Appendix Tables 7, 10, 16, 17, 18, and 19. They were not extracted because the 100-harmful-example results, explicit benign-data results, and aggregate selective-weight-recovery result suffice for the tested versions represented here; the paper's SoftSFT comparison does not measure the opening-bypass behavior in V4.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or position-wise analysis between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, suffix, or decoding-change attacks.
No test of whether data or the objective causes shallowness.
Safety-recovery/deepening data augmentation was not tested. Only the token-wise constrained fine-tuning objective (SoftSFT) was used, as a baseline under QLoRA.
Not tested whether a fixed, model-wide small set of weights or ranks carries safety independent of the particular fine-tune.

missing.what: Harmful rate after clean-data fine-tuning (0 injected) for all five models on SQL, CHEAT, SAMSum and TOXIC, plus NL2BASH for Gemma/LLaMA2. Shows no erosion for Gemma and LLaMA2.
Harmful rate after injecting 100/500/1,500 harmful pairs and 392 post-moderation pairs into each task dataset. LLaMA2 is resistant at 0.1k, and all models exceed 50% at 1.5k.
SoftSFT harmful rate vs task performance per model and dataset
Recovery harmful rate by direction-layer position, and incomplete LLaMA2 recovery
Fine-tuned harmful rates on HEx-PHI/CATQA after 1.5k injection (e.g. LLaMA2 7B SQL 94.5% on HEx-PHI)

record.verdict_notes: R1/R2 values are swapped relative to Table 6 column order (Hex, BT). The benign-data erosion claimed in the abstract and introduction rests on Mistral (and weakly Qwen); the other three models show none. All harmful judgments come from a ShieldLM-based judge, with no uncertainty reported. SoftSFT was re-implemented under QLoRA by the authors, which may weaken it.

versions.untested_parts: The paper also reports harmful-data-injection sweeps in task datasets, including 1,500 harmful examples, but those separate per-model/per-dataset outcomes are not extracted here.
Only the explicitly described benign NL2BASH results are extracted; the paper's full benign-data results across all models and datasets are not extracted.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement or response-position distribution is reported.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change bypass test is reported.
The study reports recovery using selective weight restoration, but does not establish that a particular fixed set of weights or ranks uniquely carries safety.
The paper does not test whether data or a training objective causes safety to be shallow across response tokens.
The study does not train safety to extend beyond early response tokens or test the durability of such deepening.

relation.reason: The paper directly measures safety erosion after fine-tuning, selective restoration, and the protection offered by token-constrained fine-tuning.

tranche.reason: The motivating and pure-harmful experiments repeat aligned-model fine-tuning on benign or harmful examples and measure harmful compliance.

source_check.notes: The 0.2% setting is an iterative selection rate, not the final fraction restored; selected weights depend on the fine-tuned checkpoint. The study does not establish a fixed minimal parameter set jointly necessary and sufficient across fine-tunes.

statements.correction: Table 3, clean-data column: Gemma 2B 4.6% → 3.7–4.5%; LLaMA2-7B 0.0% → 0.9% on SAMSum and 0.0% elsewhere; LLaMA2-13B 0.0% → 1.3% on NL2BASH and 0.0% elsewhere. QLoRA and the ShieldLLM-trained judge are correctly identified.
statements.problem: The claim of no erosion for clean-task LLaMA2-7B overlooks its small SAMSum increase.

statements.correction: §6.2: recovery does not reach original alignment in several LLaMA2 cases and several CHEAT/TOXIC settings; §6.5.1: recovery depends on direction-layer depth. V5 label for these conditions: limits_scope.
statements.problem: Incomplete recovery is correctly reported, but this study's successful yet condition-dependent restoration warrants limits_scope rather than challenges.
